title: Empires of AI
gist: Teaser of Ferguson, Klaassen and Schmidt's essay arguing the U.S. and China have each built a new kind of AI empire controlling models, chips, infrastructure and capital, and thereby the terms of future scientific progress.

insights.claim: China and the United States have each assembled a new kind of empire whose dominion extends over knowledge itself, not just territory, trade routes and airspace.
insights.speaker: Niall Ferguson
insights.so_what: Frames AI as imperial infrastructure, implying lasting state-backed advantages for the two AI blocs.
insights.locator: In the span of a few years

insights.claim: By controlling large language models, chips, physical infrastructure and capital, Beijing and Washington are setting the terms of all future scientific and intellectual progress.
insights.speaker: Niall Ferguson
insights.so_what: Control of the full AI stack (models, chips, data centers, capital) is the source of power, so exposure to any layer carries geopolitical weight.
insights.locator: By controlling the large language models

insights.claim: The term 'AI superpowers' is argued to fail to capture the influence and reach of the U.S. and China in AI.
insights.speaker: Niall Ferguson
insights.so_what: The authors see something larger than conventional great-power rivalry; expect empire-style dependency for third countries.
insights.locator: The term “AI superpowers” fails to capture
